method: OpenAI built-in image generation; six original narrative illustrations, inspected individually

prompts.1: Use case: illustration-story. Asset type: landscape hero illustration for the first essay of Daniel Murray's philosophical series The World That Made You. Create a remarkable, painterly yet materially precise literary illustration, wide 3:2 composition, no writing anywhere. Scene: the quiet interior of an ordinary Australian coastal home at dawn. An adult figure seen from behind stands at a timber window looking at the real street, sea and distant headland. In the window glass the reflection subtly layers a childhood doorway, earlier generations' hands and the much older geology of the headland; keep those layers coherent and delicate, like an old painting showing through a newer one. The street outside remains continuous and solid, not created by the figure's gaze. The main feeling is discovery of a world that existed before one's arrival: intimate, strange, beautiful, quietly funny through an ordinary chipped breakfast mug. Style: refined narrative oil painting with fine grain, lucid natural light, warm worn wood and deep blue distance, genuine human scale, spacious composition, rich texture without excessive detail. Avoid generic glowing brains, cosmic silhouettes, floating equations, mystical energy, typography, logos, diagrams or a collage of disconnected panels. No mathematical symbols or text. New original artwork, not a scientific reconstruction.
prompts.2: Use case: illustration-story. Asset type: landscape hero illustration for The Body You Keep Becoming, essay two of The World That Made You. Original literary illustration, wide 3:2 composition, refined narrative oil painting with tactile naturalistic detail and visible fine brushwork, warm worn wood, soft deep-blue shadows, no words or mathematical symbols. Scene: one ordinary kitchen table carries a whole lived passage through seasons. A sapling's shadow in spring, bright summer fruit, autumn leaves at an open window and a little winter condensation coexist subtly as layered light, not separate panels. On the table are a well-used cup with a carefully repaired chip, sewing materials, a loaf being broken, a child's small knitted garment and an elderly person's reading spectacles. Living hands from different ages appear naturally at the edges, caring for objects or preparing food, but one chair is empty and gently lit. The emotional center is the continual work of staying alive and the weight of someone's absence. Let the ordinary objects be memorable, surprising and human rather than decorative symbols. No hospital imagery, no anatomical diagram, no miraculous recovery, no glowing mystical body, no ghosts, no lettering, no numbers, no collage grid. This is an imaginative scene about maintenance, ageing and inheritance, not a medical claim.
prompts.3: Use case: illustration-story. Asset type: wide 3:2 landscape literary hero for The Past Arrives Through Other People. Original narrative oil painting, material precision with fine brushwork and subtle imaginative layering, warm amber light, worn earth pigments and deep blue shadows, no written text or mathematical symbols. Scene: a single public doorway in an ordinary street, seen close enough to notice the threshold worn by many feet. Its successive layers of building and repair are visible together: weathered stone, an older timber frame, a modern door and a small patched step. Several distinct living people of different ages pause or pass at the threshold, one gently handing a practical worn object to a younger person. Faint reflections in the glass suggest a workshop, a classroom and shelves of records held in common; they must remain connected to the same place rather than form separate panels. The emotional center is how language, tools and remembered arrangements reach us through others, and how unequal ease of access can be seen in a real step or door. Include a small, quietly comic improvised repair that actually helps the entrance function. Beautiful, thoughtful, spacious, human rather than grandiose. Do not imply that history inevitably improves, do not create a futuristic portal, supernatural ancestors, luminous web, infographic, diagram, flags, slogans or readable signage. No equations, numbers, labels, typography or logos.
prompts.4: Use case: illustration-story. Asset type: landscape hero for The Room to Be Wrong in a serious but mischievous philosophical essay series. Original wide 3:2 narrative oil painting with fine brushwork, highly believable worn materials, warm amber daylight, deep blue shadows and coherent human scale. Scene: an ordinary room with two open doors seen from a seated person's perspective. One door opens onto a confusing hallway; the other, revealed by a modest movable desk lamp, opens onto a practical route through a garden gate into daylight. A very grand, slightly overconfident official portrait on the wall is placed so its ornate frame nearly conceals the useful doorway. The quiet comedy is the portrait's pomp versus the humble lamp and the visible way out. Include a real chair, scattered blank papers, a worn coat and the trace of an ongoing conversation; one living adult is thoughtfully moving the lamp, not being redeemed by supernatural light. The image is about revising a view and changing a condition, not magical positive thinking. Balanced, spacious, richly textured and emotionally intelligent. No visible words, numbers, mathematics, diagrams, slogans or logos. Avoid generic glowing minds, maze symbolism, triumphal hero poses or cynical caricatures of vulnerable people.
prompts.5: Use case: illustration-story. Asset type: landscape hero for The Edge of the Map, essay five in The World That Made You. Create an original wide 3:2 literary oil painting with exceptionally rich but believable texture, deep midnight blue, moonlit slate, restrained warm lamplight and a spacious sense of wonder. Scene: a real rocky shoreline beneath a wide night sky. A single observer with a modest lantern kneels beside an unfinished hand-drawn map on a low weathered wooden board. The map contains only unlabelled coastline contours and natural texture, no words, numbers, grid or symbols. Its paper edge visually aligns with the actual coast beyond it, but the world continues clearly past the paper. Faint starlight and a distant coastal lighthouse make received light and limited viewpoint tangible. The observer is small within the landscape, engaged in work rather than a cosmic hero. Render the real coast and physical objects lucidly; any imaginative connection stays a visual metaphor, not a supposed scientific simulation. Extraordinary image through composition, material and scale, not psychedelic effects. No black-hole spectacle, galaxy inside a skull, glowing mathematical geometry, equations, text, lettering, diagrams or logos.
prompts.6: Use case: illustration-story. Create the sixth and final hero illustration for The World We Leave Behind by evolving the supplied opening-window painting. Retain the same room, timber window, recognizable coastal street, headland, perspective and refined narrative oil-painting style. Show a possible morning a generation later: a different young adult stands at the window in the same ordinary posture, holding the same recognizably worn blue-and-white mug whose chip has now been carefully repaired. A small pair of older hands at the edge of the scene is passing on a modest practical object, without showing a ghost or ancestor. Some furniture has been repaired, a plant has grown, and outside a modest shared garden and a repaired public path show consequences of earlier choices; the place is still a complex working world, not a utopia. In the glass, let old traces be fainter while the new street is clear. The emotional force should come from continuity, real change and another observer arriving, not from triumph. Make it a distinct composition in human detail while recognizably answering the opening image. No science-fiction machines, guaranteed future prediction, ethereal spirits, words, numbers, equations, logos or mathematical geometry. The scene is an original imagined future and not a forecast.

edit_03: Preserve every person, object, composition, lighting and painted texture. Remove all chalk words, numbers and symbols from the classroom blackboard; leave it blank with natural worn chalkboard texture.
usage: Imagined literary scenes, not scientific reconstructions or forecasts.
